FAA honeycomb reliability study lists an 'Ultra Image UT Scanner' and a 'MAUS' resonance scanner among participants (Galella 2006, opened; their PoD curves were charts and were not read numerically). limitations: E2580 covers flat panels with parallel surfaces only. Squirter TT needs access to both faces and water or a couplant. Water in the cells transmits sound and masks disbond. Core cell-wall paths transmit sound, so the contrast between bonded and disbonded is not binary. No kissing/weak-bond capability stated.
beryllium_notes: Be has acoustic impedance 24e6 kg/m2s against aluminium 17e6 (Materion tech brief), longitudinal velocity about 12.9 km/s, and low internal attenuation at high frequency (see record bond-beryllium-acoustic-and-xray). No source opened reports UT of a bonded Be face; the 0.8 mm face would be acoustically thin and the first echoes of the bond line would arrive earlier than for aluminium or CFRP of the same thickness. That last clause is an inference, not a sourced fact.

coverage_rate: Vendor claims only, none verified independently: Dantec Q-810 portable vacuum hood 15 m2/h ('Grosse Flaechen abscannen (15qm/hr)', slide 7, 2015); Dantec robotic system 1-2 m2/min in a vacuum chamber, delivered 2008 to a business-jet maker (2009 press release); Dantec SHS33 '~1 m2/minute' (UAH sheet quoting the vendor). Against these, the NASA field figure is 4 h for the whole 13.5 inch OD RMS tube with acoustic stressing (1995).
used_on: Space Shuttle external tank SOFI close-outs and acreage (KSC 1995; Michoud/MSFC ET-122 after Hurricane Katrina, 95 indications, 8 tanks inspected to 2010); SRB forward section MSA-2 ablator; RMS arm honeycomb; business-jet composite parts in a vacuum chamber (Dantec press release). ASTM E2581 states use on composite and metal face-sheet honeycomb and foam sandwiches.
limitations: Needs a matte, light surface and a stable article (NASA ET-122 slide 5: 'The part under test must have a matte, light colored, surface'). Fringes encode slope, so asymmetric/strip defects need two shear directions. The loading must deflect the face over the flaw: for a very stiff 0.8 mm Be face over a 3/8 inch cell the deflection per unit stress is unknown from these sources. Shuttle results are on foam, not metal faces; honeycomb result was on a thin Kevlar skin. The ET-122 team stated follow-up tactile and visual inspection was needed to confirm indications.
beryllium_notes: Be is a bright metal: shearography needs a diffuse surface (coating or paint), a surface condition requirement from the ET paper. Be face stiffness (E about 290 GPa, Materion) is higher than aluminium (70 GPa, Materion Table 1) and far higher than the Shuttle's foam or Kevlar skins, so the pressure-induced out-of-plane bulge over a disbond may be smaller; no source quantifies it. Inference only. The natural load for the sphere is the evacuation itself (a program inference, not sourced).

limitations: Detection limit is set by the face-to-core-wall thickness ratio because heat spreads laterally into the core walls; this was shown for composite faces. beryllium_notes: Be has thermal conductivity 216 W/m.K and specific heat 1.95 J/g.C (Materion SR-200). The NASA model's composite face has 0.0021 cal/cm.s.C (about 0.88 W/m.K, conversion by this worker) and its aluminium core 0.33 cal/cm.s.C. Whether high lateral conduction in a 0.8 mm Be face blurs the local thermal contrast of a disbond, and what face-to-wall thickness ratio the program's core has (cell-wall thickness not given in the task), are open questions; no thermography of a Be face was found. E2582 s5.3 says low-emissivity optically translucent surfaces may need an opaque high-emissivity coating; Be emissivity is not given in any source opened.

used_on: Radiography of brazed beryllium honeycomb sandwich panels (NASA CR-130648, 1972, panels of 10 ft2); X-ray CT of aluminium-core sandwich with CFRP faces to find core crush and skin-to-core disbond (Zalameda & Parker, opened, composite faces).
limitations: The NIST numbers show the X-ray transparency of Be, but the opposite matters here too: an aluminium core inside Be faces gives good X-ray contrast (Zalameda said aluminium honeycomb has 'excellent X-ray contrast compared to the composite face sheet'), yet X-ray is poor on thin area-type disbonds (MDPI/Li & Zhou 2019 intro: low contrast for debond defects, not independently verified here). Radiography/CT of a 20 m sphere is impractical as a field method; the CT system in the NASA paper took samples up to 25.4 x 25.4 cm.
beryllium_notes: This record is the Be note. Be is nearly X-ray transparent: NIST mass attenuation at 50 keV is 0.1554 cm2/g for Be against 0.3681 for Al, and at 20 keV 0.2251 against 3.441 (rows quoted above), so radiography can see the core and bond-line voids through the faces. High velocity (about 12.9 km/s against 6.4 km/s for aluminium, Materion Table 1) and low attenuation favour high-frequency UT inside Be; high stiffness and conductivity are the limiting factors for shearography and thermography.

resolution.value: pulse echo and through transmission, 0.5-20 MHz, flat panels with parallel surfaces
resolution.conditions: no sensitivity or flaw size in the public text; accept/reject set by contract
resolution.quote: This practice does not specify accept-reject criteria.

resolution.quantity: E2581: defect types
resolution.value: delamination, deformation under load, disbond/unbond, microcracks, thickness variation
resolution.conditions: keywords list thermal, vacuum stress and vibration stress shearography; metal-faced honeycomb stated as used with excellent results; no accept/reject criteria (s1.4)
resolution.quote: delamination, deformation under load, disbond/unbond, microcracks, and thickness variation

resolution.quantity: E2582: flaw types and 1-D heat-flow rule
resolution.value: heated area must exceed the thickness (and inspection area by 5%)
resolution.conditions: does not cover core or far-side bond; curved panels within 30 degrees of the optical axis; flaws must have aspect ratio greater than one (s5.4)
resolution.quote: of the heated area should be significantly greater than the thickness

coverage_rate: n/a
used_on: Aerospace composites and sandwich (Committee E07 practices). All three specify polymer-matrix (E2582 also ceramic-matrix) composites; none states a scope for beryllium or other metal faces except E2581's sentence on metal face sheet sandwich.
limitations: None of the three public texts gives a minimum detectable flaw size; E2580 and E2582 require flat or near-flat panels; E2582 excludes core and far-side bond; the relevant guides (E2533 for shearography) and the full texts were not read.
beryllium_notes: The standards define no Be case; E2582 explicitly says surfaces need opacity and emissivity.

missing: 1) No source found that inspects an adhesively bonded beryllium face on aluminium honeycomb by any bond-NDE method (UT, air-coupled, laser UT, shearography, thermography, tap). Only Be physical data (Materion, NIST) and radiography of an all-Be brazed honeycomb (NASA CR-130648) were found. 2) No minimum detectable disbond size for 0.8 mm metal faces over 23 mm core with 3/8 inch cells in any source opened; the closest numbers are 28-43 mm a90/95 for tap on 0.5 mm Al faces over 19 mm core (Genest 2023) and shearography on foam (POD 0.95 at debond diameter equal to foam thickness) and a Kevlar-skinned honeycomb tube (single-cell sensitivity with acoustic excitation). 3) No areal rate (m2/h) from an independent source: only vendor claims (Dantec 15 m2/h hood, 1-2 m2/min robot, ~1 m2/min) and field anecdotes. None for UT, thermography, air-coupled, laser UT, fringe projection or profilers. 4) No scarf-joint NDE source (30:1 seam), and no kissing/weak bond detection shown on honeycomb; NASA phase method only on glass coupons. 5) Lock-in thermography: no numbers read. 6) Nikon laser-radar MPE could not be downloaded (extraction only, unverified and internally inconsistent). Official Hexagon AT960 sheet not obtained (distributor copy). ZEISS/GOM/Hexagon scanner measuring-area and point-distance tables not obtained. 7) Nothing found on shape measurement of a 20 m closed evacuated sphere under external pressure, with DIC through a window or photogrammetry in vacuum. The only sphere-scale photogrammetry is the 35 m LNG tank (NBS, 1979) and its 7 mm residual scatter is dominated by the tank's own shape. 8) Documents that failed or were blocked: ROSAP FAA/Sandia honeycomb PoD report (HTTP 403), DTIC ADA201815 Fokker bondtester evaluation (403), Nikon pages (403), NASA LAR-TOPS-332 (403), Olympus BondMaster probe pages (undecodable), UArizona SCOTS dissertation (login page). 9) Downloaded but not read: ntrs 20070035909 and 20090019139 (air-coupled acoustic thermography), 20130010408, 20160007045, 20160012012, NBSIR 81-1655, arXiv 2002.12201 (NDT composites review), Materion further sheets, Hexagon StereoScan/PrimeScan pages (no spec table in extracted text). 10) Search-summary-only items not relied on: iPhoton 64 ft2/h and Lockheed F-22 duct figures (laser UT); Laser Technology 5-10 m2/h shearography (SAMPE 2004); Applied Laser 2024 honeycomb negative-pressure shearography 10 mm class; 2015 Chinese laser shearography 10 mm debond sensitivity. 11) Inferences marked as such in beryllium_notes (thermal blur, stiffer face reducing shearography deflection, acoustic thinness) are not sourced facts.
